name: Continental Blue
lede: Continental Blue is a near-black, blackish purple from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, despite the word "blue" in its name.

sections.title: A blue that reads as black
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's *A Dictionary of Color* places this hue on plate 48, cell C11, first recorded in 1927 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system classes it as a blackish purple, not a blue at all by the modern systematic name, even though the dictionary entry calls it blue [2]. The same plate carries two related names, Sailor (1923) and Sinbad (1926), both nautical [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[pale-black-shade]], [[pale-black-shade]], [[vivid-black]] and [[black-blue]], at 3.4, 3.4, 5.5 and 5.6 ΔE [1]. Say plainly that the name promises more blue than the eye finds [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this very dark color in 518 of 23,781 paintings, about 2.2 percent, as photographed [4]. It peaks in the 1820s, in 42 of 731 paintings, and in portrait painters such as Pedro Orrente, Pietro Perugino and Gustave Caillebotte, where it is likely a shadowed background or a sitter's dark coat [4]. The count is a computed match on photographed, varnished canvases, not a pigment identification [4].
